explanation: Prey species have evolved defenses to thwart predators. These include heightened senses, speed, protective armor, spines or thorns, detachable appendages (e.g., tails that break off), poisonous chemicals, camouflage, warning coloration, and flocking behavior. Mimicry is a defense where one species resembles another that has an overt defense. In Batesian mimicry, the mimic is harmless and lacks the defense of the organism it resembles. In Müllerian mimicry, different species that share a protective defense mimic each other, reinforcing the warning to predators.

questions.q: What is the difference between Batesian mimicry and Müllerian mimicry?
opts: Batesian mimicry occurs in plants, while Müllerian mimicry occurs in animals.
In Batesian mimicry, the mimic lacks the actual defense of the model; in Müllerian mimicry, the mimic shares a protective defense with other resembling species.
Batesian mimicry involves auditory signals, while Müllerian mimicry is purely visual.
In Batesian mimicry, the predator mimics the prey; in Müllerian mimicry, the prey mimics the predator.
